remediation.issue: The plugin manifest uses a parent-relative path for SKILL.md.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the target fixed and repository-local, and verify plugin-loader path restrictions before distribution.

remediation.issue: Installation documentation includes shell and PowerShell commands that can modify user directories.
remediation.suggestion: Label commands as manual steps, explain the destination, and require user confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: The report contains repeated static-analysis alerts for prose and metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Tune the scanner to distinguish documentation, manifest URLs, code examples, and executable runtime code.

content.value_statement: AI work can appear complete before the result is opened, tested, or checked against the request. This skill adds staged planning, real-environment verification, and honest completion levels.
actual_capabilities: Organizes work into five stages from ideation through discipline review.
Requires opening the delivered result in its real environment before completion.
Separates verified results from unverified paths and records remaining gaps.
Supports staged rule loading for planning, review, and multi-agent tasks.
Uses C1 and C2 completion levels to distinguish technical verification from user satisfaction.
limitations: It does not replace domain-specific tests, security review, or user acceptance.
It cannot verify an output that the model or user cannot open.
C2 product satisfaction requires user or external confirmation.
It provides workflow guidance rather than an execution engine.

use_cases.title: Review a Code Change
use_cases.description: Ask an engineer or coding agent to implement a change, run focused checks, open the result, and report verified and unverified paths.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multiple Agents
use_cases.description: Use staged planning and explicit handoffs when several agents divide research, implementation, testing, or review.

use_cases.title: Validate a Client Deliverable
use_cases.description: Track whether a document, design, or analysis matches the request and distinguish technical completion from stakeholder approval.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Completion Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Complete this task, then open the actual result and list what you verified, what remains unverified, and whether the request is complete.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first-time user needs a simple evidence-based delivery check.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Before Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan this task in clear stages. Identify the required checks and the real environment where the final result must be opened before you implement it.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants a controlled plan before asking an agent to make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Finished Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this completed change against the original request. Recalculate important numbers, open the output, test the critical path, and mark every unverified claim.
prompt_templates.scenario: An engineer needs a disciplined review of an existing deliverable.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate an Agent Team
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this project into independent agent roles. Define handoff evidence, assign a reviewer, verify the integrated result in its real environment, and report the appropriate C1 or C2 status.
prompt_templates.scenario: A technical lead is coordinating several agents on a shared deliverable.

output_examples.input: Build a small dashboard and tell me when it is finished.
output_examples.output: The dashboard is implemented. I opened it in the target environment, checked the main interaction, and verified the displayed totals. Mobile layout and external data refresh remain unverified.

output_examples.input: Have two agents research and implement this feature.
output: Research agent: documented assumptions and acceptance checks.
Implementation agent: completed the feature and supplied the changed files.
Review: opened the integrated result and checked the critical path.
Status: C1 verified; stakeholder approval is still required for C2.

output_examples.input: Confirm that this report is correct.
output_examples.output: The report matches the requested structure and its key figures were recalculated. Source freshness and business acceptance were not independently verified.

best_practices: Define the evidence required for completion before implementation begins.
Open and use the delivered result in the environment that matters.
State verified facts, unverified paths, and completion level separately.
anti_patterns: Do not declare completion from code inspection alone.
Do not treat a green check as proof that the guarded failure case works.
Do not label a result C2 without user or external confirmation.

faq.question: What does this skill verify?
faq.answer: It verifies delivery evidence, real-environment use, critical checks, and honest reporting of remaining uncertainty.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides the agent to choose and run relevant checks, but available tools and project tests determine execution.

faq.question: What is C1?
faq.answer: C1 means the technical delivery was checked with available evidence, while some broader acceptance may remain open.

faq.question: What is C2?
faq.answer: C2 means the product is satisfactory, which requires user or external confirmation rather than model judgment alone.

faq.question: Can it coordinate multiple agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports role separation, explicit handoffs, review evidence, and integrated-result verification.

faq.question: Which tools support it?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, plus compatible clients that follow the same skill convention.
